name: form
behavior: None — native <form> semantics. APG form/validation guidance: every control has an accessible name from its label (for/id), description and error are wired through aria-describedby, an invalid control carries aria-invalid, and the error text is announced (role=alert). Submission never relies on colour alone to signal failure; focus moves to the first invalid control.

parts.note: the <form> element; stacks field items and the submit row
one labelled control with its description/message — the same stack as the field anatomy, owned by the form so validation state can flow from the form model

parts.statesNote: invalid renders in status-critical; disabled renders in content-disabled per states.md

parts.note: hosts any form control anatomy (input, textarea, select, checkbox, radio-group, switch, slider); receives id/aria-describedby/aria-invalid from the item — no tokens of its own
validation message; replaces the description while the control is invalid

anatomyNotes: Intersection of shadcn Form (FormItem/FormLabel/FormControl/FormDescription/FormMessage over react-hook-form) and Salt FormField (FormField/FormFieldLabel/FormFieldHelperText). Salt merges description and validation message into ONE helper-text part whose tone changes with validationStatus; shadcn keeps them separate and swaps at render time. The registry keeps them as two parts and renders only one at a time — a superset that both themes can express. Salt's necessityLabel (optional/required suffix on the label) is a RECIPE addition inside the label part, not a part. The form-state binding library (react-hook-form) is an implementation choice, never anatomy: the parts are identical for uncontrolled forms.
